messages.subject: Issue with micro_global function
parts:
Hi there,

I've been working with the function micro_global, and it sunddenly stopped working followed by:

> micro<-micro_global(loc="Melbourne, Australia")

OVER_QUERY_LIMIT:Melbourne,Australia
[1] "try 2 ..."
OVER_QUERY_LIMIT:Melbourne,Australia
[1] "try 3 ..."
OVER_QUERY_LIMIT:Melbourne,Australia
[1] "try 4 ..."
OVER_QUERY_LIMIT:Melbourne,Australia
extracting climate data

Error in CLIMATE[, 1] : incorrect number of dimensions

>

I tried to reinstall NicheMapR, and even the R, but no success. Could someone help me out, please?

All the best,

Rodolfo

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Issue with micro_global function
parts:
Dear Rodolfo,

I noticed this recently too - it is to do with the geocode function in dismo, which connects to the Google Earth API. There has been a change in the API - you might have to register, see: https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/

However, if you give the micro_global function a longitude and latitude it will work.

All the best,
Mike

messages.author: 5481ac51bfcf2936
messages.subject: Re: Issue with micro_global function
parts:
Hi Mike,

Many thanks for the very quick reply! Indeed, micro_global worked when I typed the longitude and latitude.

Cheers!

All the best,

Rodolfo
